mappings.note: Asks which landform the pupil's own town sits in and which chapter features are visible around it - identifying India's mountains, plateaus or plains in the real setting, which is LO-32. Not LO-33, since no map is drawn.
Describe the plateau, plain and mountain met on the Chhota Nagpur to Prayagraj to Almora route; three named Indian physical features, squarely LO-32.

Pairs Indian pilgrimage places with the landform each stands in, so the demand is to place Indian mountains, plateaus and plains. Not LO-35, whose sites are historical sources for reconstructing the past, not places of worship.

A true/false set spanning Himalayan summits, plateau edges, river tributaries and fertile sediment (LO-32) as well as desert flora and fauna (LO-27). Both are needed; no single outcome carries the whole item.
Matching set mixing Indian features (Gangetic plains, Ganga, Yamuna) under LO-32 with world features (Kilimanjaro to Africa, the Tibetan plateau as roof of the world) under LO-30.
Defines 'landform' as a natural physical feature - the vocabulary LO-32 is built on, since it is the only outcome naming mountains, plateaus and plains.
The three-way classification into mountains, plateaus and plains, which is exactly the list LO-32 enumerates. Not LO-27, no life is involved.

Altitude as height above mean sea level - the measure by which the landforms of LO-32 are distinguished. Deliberately not LO-31: altitude is not a latitude or longitude, though the distractors invite that error.
Mountain snowmelt feeding rivers links two of LO-32's named features. Not LO-27, because the item stops at where the water goes rather than at what it supports.
Defines precipitation, a movement of water between the earth's zones, which is LO-27's subject. Not LO-32: no landform is named.
Picks the Himalayas out of the Alps, Andes and Atlas by continent - a world-map ranges question, so LO-30. The India-specific Himalayan items in this chapter are mapped to LO-32 instead.
Kanchenjunga on the Nepal-Sikkim border; an Indian mountain to be placed on the map of India. Not LO-30, since the item is about a peak within India rather than a continent.
Asks which CONTINENT Kilimanjaro stands on, so the answer is a continent on the world map - LO-30, not the Indian-features outcome.
Anamudi as South India's highest peak - a named Indian mountain, so LO-32 rather than the world-map outcome used for Kilimanjaro.
Montane forest and its conifers is plant life adapted to a zone of the earth, which is the biosphere reference in LO-27. Not LO-32, because no landform has to be located.
Vegetation above the tree line - grasses, mosses and lichens - is again the biosphere, paired with the montane-forest item and distinct from the pure landform questions.

Landslide risk for people living in the mountains is about the earth as a human habitat, which only the goal CG-SST1 states; LO-27 is narrower (life and the biosphere) and LO-32 is about locating features, so neither outcome fits a hazard-to-people question.
Defines a plateau by its flat top and raised edges - the plateau term in LO-32's list, contrasted here with mountains and plains.
Black soil on lava plateaus is a property of the plateau landform. Not LO-47, because the item asks for the soil type, not for the farming that follows from it.
Hundru Falls on the Subarnarekha - an Indian river and plateau edge to be placed on the map of India, so LO-32.
How rivers build floodplains by depositing sediment; the formation of one of LO-32's named features. Not LO-47, since no occupation is asked about.

Why plains support crop farming: the question is about the availability of agriculture as an occupation (LO-47), grounded in the plain's fertile soil (LO-32). Kept apart from the pure floodplain-formation item, which stops at the landform.
Over-irrigation depleting groundwater is a cost of the farming occupation of the plains (LO-47) paid in one of the earth's water stores (LO-27). Not LO-32, since no landform is being located.
Defines a confluence - river vocabulary, and rivers are named in LO-32. Not LO-30, which is about continents and oceans.
Gentle plain gradients making rivers navigable and so supporting transport and trade - a livelihood consequence (LO-47) of a landform property (LO-32).

The five tinais of Sangam poetry is a fact drawn from an ancient literary work, which LO-36 covers. Not LO-32, because the item asks about the poetry's classification rather than about India's actual landforms.

Kurinji as the mountain tinai and its hunting-and-gathering life, again content described in Sangam literature. Not LO-38, whose hunting-gathering stage is a prehistoric development, not a poetic landscape.
That landforms take millions of years to form is a fact about the mountains, plateaus and plains of LO-32, not about life or about a map skill.
Distinguishes mountain from hill by height and steepness - a discrimination within LO-32's landform vocabulary.
Matches a mountain range to its continent (Andes to South America); a world-map continent item, so LO-30 rather than the India outcome.

Terrace farming as the method that suits a steep slope - how the landform decides the form the farming occupation takes, which is LO-47. Not LO-32: the item asks about the practice, not about the mountain.
Assertion that plateaus are storehouses of minerals (LO-32) with mining as the major economic activity there as the reason (LO-47). The item is built on the link, so both are cited.

The Tibetan Plateau's height earns it 'Roof of the World', but it is not one of India's physical features, so LO-32 would be a misfit and LO-30 covers only continents and oceans; the competency is the honest altitude for a plateau outside India.
Rules out cities as a landform and keeps mountains, plateaus and plains - testing exactly the set LO-32 names as natural features.
Fine sediments as the source of floodplain fertility; a property of the plain landform, mapped like the other formation items rather than to the agriculture outcome.
Matches Neydal to the coastal landscape of Sangam poetry - literary content, so LO-36 with the other tinai items.
Identifies a desert from low rainfall (LO-32 names deserts) AND from its specially adapted sparse vegetation (LO-27). Both clauses are load-bearing in the stem.
Sharp peaks as the mark of geologically young mountains - a mountain property under LO-32, the counterpart of the mountain-versus-hill item.
Places Hundru and Jog Falls on plateau edges, linking Indian rivers to the plateau landform; LO-32 covers both.
